clue.text: Collided with second vehicle

parts.note: a truck is a goods vehicle

explanation.surface: A driver reports a crash involving a second vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To have hit something is to have crashed into it.

clue.text: Aces turned up daily, at first, in these intervals

indicators.note: at first says the turned newspaper comes before the word for aces
in a down clue, turned up means the word for daily is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: The Times is a daily newspaper
aces in cards count as ones

explanation.surface: A card player marvels at aces turning up every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' makes SEMIT from TIMES, and 'at first' puts it ahead of ONES. The daily is the newspaper this crossword appears in.
explanation.definitionFit: In music these are the smallest steps between notes on a Western scale, half a whole tone each.

clue.text: Most affluent state seen on the box

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
a chest is a large box

explanation.surface: The wealthiest state is the one shown on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the box' suggests television, but here it is a chest; 'seen on' simply places RI before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The richest person has the greatest wealth, a superlative of wealthy.

clue.text: Overall success for show-jumper

parts.note: in show-jumping a round with no fences knocked and no refusals is the complete success a rider wants

explanation.definitionFit: A faultless show-jumping round, with no penalties incurred, is a whole-course triumph.

clue.text: Record pile, perhaps, for the following person

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of pile are offered in some other possible arrangement

explanation.surface: A stack of vinyl records is set aside for the next person in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals the anagram of the second piece; 'the following person' reads as whoever comes next, but means a follower.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciple is a follower of a teacher or leader.

clue.text: In Priestley play he calls for one, script revision

indicators.note: a revision reworks text, so the letters of one and script are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatre director revises the script of a Priestley play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision' shuffles ONE and SCRIPT together. J. B. Priestley's play is An Inspector Calls, whose title character arrives to question a family.
explanation.definitionFit: The visiting police investigator is the figure who calls in Priestley's drama, as the title says.

clue.text: It's a coastal feature, old chap

explanation.surface: A beach-side bay is described as if it were an old fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sheltered bay on a coastline, and a dated British slang word for a man or fellow.

clue.text: Capital becoming a problem — disheartened?

indicators.note: becoming signals the letters turning into something new, an anagram

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: disheartened removes the central letter, the heart, of the word problem

explanation.surface: A city turning into a headache leaves people dejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the middle B of PROBLEM, leaving PROLEM; 'becoming' then rearranges A plus PROLEM.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital of Sicily, a regional capital city in Italy.

clue.text: Rival soldiers in the old rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the assembled letters are read upwards
in places the word for soldiers inside the old word for the

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the
men is a common word for soldiers

explanation.surface: An opponent's troops took part in an uprising long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' builds YMENE and 'rising' turns it upwards, as befits a down clue. YE is the old spelling of 'the' seen in signs like Ye Olde Shoppe.
explanation.definitionFit: A rival is an opponent or foe in conflict.

clue.text: She's beside herself in the great heat he adores

indicators.note: in shows the name lies inside the words that follow, spanning their breaks

explanation.surface: A woman is overcome by passion in the summer's great heat.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs through greaT HEAt and again straight after it in THE Adores, so she is literally beside herself.
explanation.definitionFit: Thea is a woman's name, so it can stand for a female person.

clue.text: Title role — don't mention it to other actors

definitions.text: Title role — don't mention it to other actors

parts.words: Title role — don't mention it to other actors
parts.note: theatrical superstition forbids saying the name of Shakespeare's Scottish play inside a theatre, so actors call it the Scottish play

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Scottish king gives his name to the play actors superstitiously avoid naming.

clue.text: Spanish article is put back here in Spain

indicators.note: put back means the whole string of letters is reversed

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
to be, or exist, is to live: is = lives

explanation.surface: A Spanish newspaper piece is returned to its home city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses EL plus LIVES as a single run.
explanation.definitionFit: Seville is a city in southern Spain, so it is a place 'here' in that country.

clue.text: Divorce? One may put an end to close match

definitions.text: One may put an end to close match

explanation.surface: A divorce is set beside a sports decider, both ending something.
explanation.definitionFit: A divorce breaks the marriage tie; in tennis an extra game decides a set at six-all.

clue.text: Cause irritation in brawl

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up trouble in a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To fray is to wear thin someone's nerves, and a fray is also a noisy fight.

clue.text: Be found around new training ship

indicators.note: new tells us to make a fresh arrangement of the letters of be and training

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recruit is found to be around a ship for new training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found around' joins, and 'new' is the anagram signal; 'training ship' reads as one phrase, but only 'ship' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigantine is a two-masted sailing vessel, square-rigged on the foremast.

clue.text: Well-connected group in the fishing industry?

explanation.surface: A contact circle is compared to fishermen's jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of linked people or computers; and, playfully, labour with nets in fishing.

clue.text: Child, note, really likes gentle handlers

parts.note: a kid is a child
G is a musical note
to love is to really like

explanation.surface: A child, notably, adores people who treat others softly.
explanation.walkthrough: To handle someone 'with kid gloves' is to treat them very gently.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft goatskin gloves, figuratively the delicate treatment used in tactful dealing.

clue.text: Dismiss number of people assembled

explanation.surface: A crowd's size is set beside a dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn out is to expel someone; and a turnout is the attendance at an event.

clue.text: Crosses lines — putting train, first, in shed

indicators.note: first says what is left of train goes at the start
in shed means the letters i and n are cast off from the word train

parts.note: verses are lines of poetry

explanation.surface: A train crosses rail lines and is put first into the engine shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a railway building for the train, but it means cast off; 'putting ... first' orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To travel across an area is to go from one side to the other.

clue.text: Rotund characters in all directions — many passed out

indicators.note: in places the round letters inside the four compass points

parts.note: the four compass points S, W, N and E cover every direction
O is the roundest letter, so two rotund characters are two Os
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number

explanation.surface: Plump people scattered everywhere as many fainted.
explanation.walkthrough: The round letters OO sit inside S W N E, then D finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To faint is to lose consciousness, collapsing as if overcome.

clue.text: Perform better, but not in dramatic scenes

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
a play is a drama made up of scenes

explanation.surface: An actor does better, though not when in dramatic scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat an opponent through superior skill in a game.

clue.text: Main events.

parts.note: the main is the sea, so its events are boat races held on the water

explanation.definitionFit: A series of boat races, contests that take place on open water.

clue.text: This imaginary animal went to .. man's head

definitions.text: This imaginary animal went to .. man's head

parts.words: This imaginary animal went to .. man's head
parts.note: like a unicorn but three-horned, the beast's name is also an eighteenth-century three-pointed hat worn on a man's head

explanation.definitionFit: A three-cornered cocked hat, and by analogy with unicorn a fabled three-horned creature.

clue.text: Obligation avoided by some who take flight

definitions.text: avoided by some who take flight

explanation.surface: Air passengers dodge a tax they owe.
explanation.definitionFit: A duty is a moral obligation and also a customs tax, escaped by buying goods free of it at airports.

clue.text: Fact US lawyer needed to stem-ach

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor
the clue's stem-ach is the word stomach broken across a line, and tum is an informal word for stomach

explanation.surface: An American prosecutor must swallow an inconvenient truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed to' joins; the second piece is the noun stomach, split by a hyphen in print, not the verb meaning tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single piece of information or given item.

clue.text: Fruit, my darling?

explanation.surface: Someone calls a citrus fruit their sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: A small citrus like a tangerine; and the girl of the old song Oh My Darling, Clementine.

clue.text: May, for example, be listlessly idle

explanation.surface: May, the month, is described as lazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A month is a lunar cycle, so May is one; and to moon about is to drift aimlessly.

clue.text: Surplus further increased by extra, perhaps

explanation.surface: A surplus grows further with something extra.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls, and an extra such as a wide or no-ball adds another delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: Excess left beyond what is needed; and the cricket set of deliveries lengthened when a no-ball is bowled.

clue.text: After examination, allowed back to port on Med

indicators.note: back means the whole run of letters is read in reverse
after puts the word for allowed behind the word for examination

parts.note: a viva is an oral examination at university
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: After an exam, a student is allowed back to a Mediterranean port.
explanation.walkthrough: VIVA then LET gives VIVALET, which 'back' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Tel Aviv is an Israeli city on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Threatening nothing less, being out of love

parts.note: O stands for zero, nothing

indicators.note: being out of means the word for less sits outside the letter for love

parts.note: minus means less
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Someone threatening nothing less falls out of love.
explanation.walkthrough: MINUS goes round O to give MINOUS, after the first O.
explanation.definitionFit: Something menacing suggests trouble to come.

clue.text: Nothing short of hero worship for this official

definitions.text: Nothing short of hero worship for this official

parts.words: Nothing short of hero worship for this official
parts.note: hero with its O, nothing, cut short becomes her, and Worship is a mayor's title, so her title is the form of address for this civic office-holder

explanation.definitionFit: The female mayor, or a mayor's wife, is addressed as Her Worship.

clue.text: Boy fell back

indicators.note: back says the word for fell is read in reverse

parts.note: to fall from grace is to have sinned

explanation.surface: A boy took a tumble backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dennis is a man's first name, so it can stand for a boy.
